rv.q: Pulitzer Prize winner burns bright enough to scorch but also to illuminate.
Benedict Andrews offers a brilliant, lacerating account of the play that jolts you out of any complacent sense of cosy familiarity with the dramatist's characteristic terrain.
It’s well acted, stylishly presented and very nicely, erm, tackled: preferred over 9 out of 10 Cats, you might say.

Especially in the first act, Miller puts a keenly sardonic topspin on many of her lines and successfully keeps the whole business going at a decent pace, given how much of the talking Maggie has to do in the face of near-silence from her husband Brick.

This Tennessee Williams play needs not just to feel as hot as the American South on a summer's day, it needs to sizzle. Sienna Miller as Maggie provides exactly that in the first half, bursting into the bedroom she shares with her husband, Brick, who is in the shower, naked except for his glass of whiskey. "Brick," she purrs, "I'm a cat."
This is the bleakest, most Lear-like of visions, fully rendered in this innovative and powerfully acted production.

cn.t: Miller sizzles in this stylish but uneven revival that divides critics. Andrews' contemporary update and strong lead performances draw praise, though some find the production muddled and inconsistent across its three acts.
